title: Weil conjectures I: rationality and Euler product
statement:
Let $X_0$ be a scheme of finite type (quasi-compact and locally of finite
type) over $\Fq$. Then there are $A,B\in\Z[T]$ with $B(0)=1$ and
$B(T)\,Z(X_0,T)=A(T)$ in $\Q[[T]]$; in particular
$Z(X_0,T)\in1+T\Z[[T]]\cap\Q(T)$. Moreover
$Z(X_0,T)=\prod_{x\in|X_0|}(1-T^{\deg(x)})^{-1}$ in $\Q[[T]]$, the product
over the closed points of $X_0$.

proof.text: Apply [sk-thm-rationality] to the given $X_0$. Its hypotheses are exactly that $X_0$ is quasi-compact and locally of finite type over $\Fq$, as assumed here; no separatedness, smoothness or properness is needed. It supplies $A,B\in\Z[T]$ with $B(0)=1$ and $B(T)Z(X_0,T)=A(T)$ in $\Q[[T]]$, and also $Z(X_0,T)\in\Q(T)\cap(1+T\Z[[T]])$. Thus the integral polynomial presentation and the rationality-and-integrality clause of the statement hold. The order of the two sets in the intersection does not affect membership.

source.place: The sole proof paragraph, first clause: Combine the rationality of [sk-thm-rationality].

proof.text: For $X_0$ of finite type the zeta series of [sk-def-zeta] and of [def-weil-point-counts-zeta] coincide. Both are $\exp(\sum_{n\geq1}N_nT^n/n)$ with $N_n=\#\operatorname{Hom}_{\Fq}(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf F_{q^n},X_0)$. The field $\mathbf F_{q^n}$ is the splitting field of $T^{q^n}-T$ over $\Fq$ in the first and the subfield of $k$ with $q^n$ elements in the second; these are isomorphic $\Fq$-algebras, so the two Hom sets are in bijection. The convention of [sk-def-zeta] that $N_n=0$ when the set is infinite never applies, since [def-weil-point-counts-zeta] states that these sets are finite for finite-type $X_0$. Both nodes define $\deg(x)=[\kappa(x):\Fq]$. Thus the notation in the item and in [prop-euler-product] refers to the same series and degrees. Apply [prop-euler-product] with $Y_0=X_0$, again using precisely the finite-type hypothesis. Its displayed consequence gives $Z(X_0,T)=\prod_{x\in|X_0|}(1-T^{\deg(x)})^{-1}\in1+T\mathbf Z[[T]]$, where $|X_0|$ denotes the closed points and $\deg(x)=[\kappa(x):\Fq]$ as in the statement. The cited proposition states that this product is coefficientwise locally finite, so the displayed identity is an identity of formal series in $\Q[[T]]$, as required. Together with the first step, this proves every assertion.

lean.statement: theorem Hom.zetaSeries_rational_and_eulerProduct {k : Type u} [Field k] [Finite k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [QuasiCompact f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] : (∃ A B : Polynomial ℤ, B.coeff 0 = 1 ∧ (B.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ) : PowerSeries ℚ) * f.zetaSeries = (A.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ) : PowerSeries ℚ)) ∧ ((∃ Z : PowerSeries ℤ, PowerSeries.constantCoeff Z = 1 ∧ PowerSeries.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ) Z = f.zetaSeries) ∧ (∃ P Q : Polynomial ℚ, Q.coeff 0 ≠ 0 ∧ (Q : PowerSeries ℚ) * f.zetaSeries = (P : PowerSeries ℚ))) ∧ f.zetaSeries = ∏' x : closedPoints X, (1 - PowerSeries.X ^ f.degreeOver x.1 : PowerSeries ℚ)⁻¹
